title: Tenant and active-event scoping is missing from the principal and several global selectors

original_titles.title: No tenant scoping in admin API; cross-tenant queries are not rejected (spec 1.6, patch E.4/R-36)
Event/stage resolution ignores the caller's event (latest-wins across all events)

problem: Principal has no tenant_id. Admin event creation selects the first tenant globally, many admin queries accept only an event_id, and state/auth/rules resolution selects the latest active event rather than the caller’s event. In a multi-tenant or multi-event deployment this can expose or mutate another tenant/event’s records.
impact: Cross-tenant data disclosure, wrong-event rules acceptance, and cross-event stage/leaderboard state. The current seed appears single-tenant, which reduces immediate exploitability but does not make the data boundary correct.

evidence_paths: backend/app/routers/admin.py: create_event, participant/team/config and export query paths
verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Add tenant_id to Principal and populate it from the joined app.users row in get_principal. Treat it as server-derived identity, never as a request parameter.

Introduce shared query helpers such as require_event_in_tenant(session, event_id, principal.tenant_id) and require_stage_in_tenant(...). Apply them before every event/stage/team/challenge/participant/dispute/export/audit mutation and read.

Change event creation to use principal.tenant_id instead of SELECT first tenant. Add tenant_id conditions to list/read/update/delete SQL and verify related objects belong to the same event and tenant.
Require an explicit selected event context for /state, /me, rules acceptance, announcements and leaderboard. Do not resolve active event using ORDER BY created_at DESC globally.

Add a second-tenant test fixture and attempt GET, PATCH, DELETE, export and participant registration using IDs from the other tenant. All cross-tenant attempts must return the same non-enumerating 404/403 policy.

acceptance_criteria: Every admin query is tenant constrained at the DB predicate, not merely checked in the UI.
A second-tenant integration test proves cross-tenant reads and writes fail.
Two concurrent active events return their own state and rules to their own participants.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.

dependencies: Tenant-aware test fixtures and DB constraints
